chunks: And with the first chain of narration from ʿAlī ibn Mahzyār, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from ʿAjlān Abū Ṣāliḥ, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, peace be upon them both, said to me:

Be just with people in your personal matters, share your wealth with them, choose for them what you choose for yourself, remember Allah abundantly, and beware of laziness and boredom; for indeed my father counseled me with that, and his father counseled him with that. And likewise regarding the night prayer:

Indeed, if you are lazy, you will not fulfil Allah’s right; and if you are discontented, you will not fulfil anyone’s right. And upon you is truthfulness, piety, and returning that which is entrusted to you; and when you make a promise, do not break it.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq advise about justice, remembrance of Allah, and keeping promises?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq (AS) instructs Ajlān Abū Ṣāliḥ with ethical counsel passed down through the Imams: be just, share wealth, remember Allah constantly, avoid laziness and boredom (which prevent fulfilling rights), maintain truthfulness, guard piety, return trusts, and keep promises. The counsel particularly emphasizes the night prayer and its connection to diligence in fulfilling obligations. This is a direct, personal exhortation that the Imam traces back through his father to his grandfather, stressing its importance as an inherited spiritual legacy.
